## Why visit

One of the best choices for combining a spectacular pub interior with a proper meal. The green ceramic arches, tiled surfaces and fireplace make the long succession of rooms unusually memorable. The cask selection is smaller than at the city’s specialist free houses, but the whole experience is exactly relevant to a trip built around traditional pubs and food. Book a table if eating, and make time to look at the bar and dining spaces rather than treating the visit solely as a restaurant reservation.

## Beer

CAMRA reports cask handpumps in the front and main rooms, with four of six in use at survey; regional and established British beers feature.

## Cider and perry

**Real-cider offering not established.** No current real-cider evidence established; ask for the producer and product at the bar.

See [how cider is classified](../real-cider.md).

## Food

Traditional British cooking and Sunday service; the operator publishes current seasonal menus. Book if this is your main meal.

## Plan the visit

Popular around Royal Exchange performances. Check the current menu and reservation availability rather than assuming a particular dish.

**Getting there:** Central Cross Street; walk from Exchange Square or Market Street and combine with Cafe Beermoth.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
